post_title: Stop Packing Up Before The Lectures Over
flattened_content:
Post Title: Stop Packing Up Before The Lectures Over
Post Body: Some of these professors are really great people happy to teach what they like to teach, and whike theyre still teaching, with about 15 minutes of lecture remaining, people start packing up. I get you wanna go but just wait the couple minutes out, it's insanely disrespectful to the professors who enjoy teaching and are passionate about it and makes it seem as if we dont care abt the class and just want to leave. Now if the professor sucks that's a while different thing, but cmon guys, basic respect.
Comment by SusheeMonster: It's also good to be mindful of how much you take out of your bag, in the first place

Packing up your textbook & laptop at the end of class is less of a hassle than your textbook,  laptop, phone, water bottle, snacks, piss pass ...
Comment by Illustrious-Group-95: Well, piss pass is not relatable for most students. According to Rutgers' recent stat publication, only 27% of students purchase it.
Comment by 90kPing: They need to do something about the illegal pissing
Comment by StealthNider: they only have enough for 27% of the students though 😭😭
Comment by Illustrious-Group-95: Sounds like a you issue, not the school's. They come out early so everyone can get them before the semester.
Comment by StealthNider: dawg it doesn’t matter when they come out if there isn’t enough in the first place
Comment by reddit-trk: 76.8% of all statistics are made-up. And the remaining 59.7% are plainly wrong.
Comment by Couple_of_wavylines: Wtf is a piss pass?
Comment by Admirable-Resident72: don't listen to them😭😭
Comment by baronmunchausen2000: It's also insanely disrespectful to the parents who pay their tuition.
Comment by ScarletGingerrr: Basic respect doesn't really apply when you're getting shoved off buses if you go right as class ends and cant go to stuff that actually matters like a more important class or your job. Sometimes you gotta set priorities and ensure you can make it places on time and if you gotta game leaving class early for a solid non-crowded bus experience then that's your call.
Comment by diiannamariie: Yes, I can totally see this and understand the circumstances, however, I highly doubt the entire class is in this predicament. I have some back to back classes and a job that falls right after a few so I pack up a minute or two early to be ready to go when they let us out. I do it quietly and haven’t taken out every unnecessary item in my bag. I swear in every class, every time, one person starts loudly packing up and then next thing you know, I can barely hear the professor over the sound of rustling papers, fast zippers, and practically slamming laptops and bags on the table. This has always been a pet peeve and until this post, never realized it was also distracting to others.
Comment by ScarletGingerrr: I can agree with that the entire class isn't in that predicament. However I feel like you said it really is just one person making a big scene and everything else, its just an overlap of sounds of people trying to leave respectfully but also 90% of the time its like the last 3 minutes of class where not much typically happens. Of course it happens like with 10 minutes left too sometimes but in my 4 years I've rarely seen it be that big of an issue that far before class ends, its always been like that last 3-5 minutes I guess I'm lucky to not have seen that occur. It is a distraction but a fleeting one. (With the exception of people making a scene like really loud music or opening some snacks even before their out the door. I agree that yeah that's something different) An also with all these people leaving early, the responsibility is on the student to learn the material to have their own success and so if they want to leave early that's their choice. Its just a really unfortunate circumstance where people try to be as quiet as they can but small noises just overlap to something big.  I agree it can get distracting but I don't think its as big of a deal and especially as classes continue throughout the semester it'll be less of an issue and especially not as frequent with attendance for most classes dropping a good 70-80%.
Comment by diiannamariie: I do agree that’s it’s not really a big deal, more of a minor annoyance lol. Funny story: I’ll never forget a kid in my Intro to Philosophy class that ate his lunch every day at the end of class and would always crinkle his chip bag (always had a giant bag, curse his skinny self haha) and get up to throw out his garbage as we were all still engaging in debate. It was annoying but we all just shrugged it off and whoever was speaking would just stop talking or a few seconds and resume after the loud crinkles and the loud plop from tossing his usually still half full Gatorade bottle, hitting the bin at Mach force, ended. I figured, okay, maybe this is the only time he has to get some food down- it is what it is, we’ve acclimated and the professor gave up trying to tell him to do it quietly. Then we found out that it was his only class that day (80 mins) and he got picked up directly after from his dad. I know, that’s an outlier but I just thought it was a relevant funny situation as some people reallllly just don’t have personal awareness sometimes.  So yes, if it’s a bunch of people doing things quietly, I don’t see an issue. I just seem to end up with classmates that are not quiet about it lol.
Comment by ScarletGingerrr: That's actually funny lol. Bro casually eating in his one and only class of the day rather than going home and doing it. Honestly the characters Rutgers brings in never fails to amaze me. I definitely have seen a good amount of teachers where its no food in class so I guess props to that professor for handling it so well(?)
Comment by reddit-trk: Yet, two "wrongs" don't make one "right."
Comment by ScarletGingerrr: Its not necessarily wrong, just multiple perspectives to one small issue. And at the end of the day, the world moves on, the sun shines another day, a minor inconvenience is forgotten and soon replaced by another one. Shit happens, 99% of it isn't a big deal, you move on with your life. Whether you choose to go to class and how long you decide to stay is on you, you're responsible for your life and it doesn't have to necessarily line up with "the common thought."
Comment by ScarletGingerrr: It really is all about if you make a big scene or not. If you're making unnecessary noise like opening a bag of chips that's a different thing but if you're trying to leave quietly then its not a big bother and especially depending on the classroom layout, its hard to avoid going in front of the professor, even if you duck down. And the respect is a two way street, of course some people think you have to stay the whole time and respect the professor coming out to teach but also the other side is that we all have lives and also learn differently and so its about setting priorities and doing the best for you. If you learn better in a different style than the professor uses and need to leave because of it, that's valid too and so it's also about realizing that the professor's lecture isn't the be all end all.
And a good 99% of professors aren't too bothered by people leaving early since they've had it happen so much if they are a long time professor or also just know that this isn't high school anymore. We're all adults and so how we learn and what we do with our time is our responsibility, if we want to succeed we'll take action for it and the professor isn't going to waste their time trying to babysit us and keep us locked down.
Comment by mrs_undeadtomato: Idk man, I start packing 5 minutes before class ends, like laptop and water bottle in my bag, if I have a bus to catch to my next class. I always wait till we are dismissed but yeah, I don't think there's anything wrong with packing a bit early if you got somewhere else to be. I typically get along with all my professors tho, so if I don't have any classes or somewhere to be I will wait till we are dismissed to leave. Just use common sense.
Comment by xavlenn: no bc its incredibly distracting and overstimulating when the entire lecture is packing up and ur prof is speedrunning 15 slides to complete the lecture in the last 10 min of class 😵‍💫
Comment by Agitated_Cook_9120: I said this yesterday I had such an amazing professor and he was shy people just kept leaving I sat through the whole 2.5 hours it was interesting yes I was tired but I also wanted to learn. Hell he even messed up on names and these so called adults had the nerve to laugh smh I hate it
Comment by DisciplinePure4352: I agree; I don't judge anyone who does this, but it's true, one should wait until the professors finish speaking bc it's disrespectful otherwise.
Comment by Murky_Implement_9826: THANK YOU. Like I’m trying to hear what she’s going to say, not the freaking zips of book bags
Comment by JNerdGaming: you right
Comment by royaljellyfish: The same goes for the crappy professors. Try and be respectful period
Comment by Aggressive-Peak-3644: whos ur favorite professor so far
Comment by AssociationDizzy1336: I did this, but only because about 30 minutes in I realized I did not understand the lecture at all. I take paper notes and the professor had already gone through 10 detailed slides 3 of which I forgot to screenshot, so I would just be writing gibberish and hurting my head even more.

I was so lost and there was three guys staring at me (I guess cause I was on my phone) and also cause the professor said they would post the slides later.

I tried to wait for when the professor was looking down.
Comment by awhitelamb: Basic respect is when you don’t grade me on participation when I’m a grown ass adult that could be held legally liable and charged as an adult. Participation isn’t the point of university. I wouldn’t even come to the class in the first place and instead choose to stay in the library studying the material than wasting solid hours not understanding or trying to catch up with the lecture. When I’m packing, I’m thanking god that I can back to real work. I’ve barely ever had any benefit from lectures. Most of these lectures are a quick recap of the material. Do you know how many times I can rewind a YouTube video? Do you know how many times I rewind? One hour video is like a three-4 hour study marathons for me. Instead of wasting my time driving to attend lecture, I could’ve used that time and energy burying myself in the library and actually doing what students should be doing. Studying. Signed, a broke engineering student that doesn’t have time or money to care for your respect when I’d be more advantaged to stay in the library studying.
Comment by jackospades88: >Signed, a broke engineering student that doesn’t have time or money to care for your respect when I’d be more advantaged to stay in the library studying

You're not going to be able to lock yourself away when you get into the real world and will need to interact with real people. Your time is not any more valuable than the other people in the room.

Signed, an engineering grad.
Comment by awhitelamb: Thanks for the advice master Oogway, anyways, have my 2cents on the matter, peace.
Comment by [deleted]: Attending class kind of is the point of having a class with a lecture. Honestly, if that style of teaching is such a mismatch to your learning style, you may want to consider switching to a different school that is more aligned with how you prefer to learn. It kind of sounds like you might do better with an online school set up or some other school more geared towards self tutoring.
Comment by awhitelamb: I love this passive agressive boot, If ya don't like it you can leave reply. Bro, most people in college come for the receipt. I have the reciept name of Rutgers. You think I'm paying for the lectures when I have it all on youtube or a book? You're telling me you're actually paying all this money for these lectures? How holy are your professors cause I need to sign up for their class. I'm paying money for this societal pressure of getting a named university degree, a.k.a. a receipt. If not, I'd just do what every engineering student actually cares for, internships and projects to place on my resume.
Comment by [deleted]: What do you mean passive aggressive? I'm addressing you directly and offering something other than the pressure to go get a Rutgers degree. I'm saying if you don't like it, it may be worth considering leaving for elsewhere. But yea if you don't even care about the degree and get go for it because others are pressuring you to do so and just want to learn, then I'd suggest considering pursuing that, resisting the pressure.  But if you just want a receipt, I'm saying there are other schools that offer receipts without lectures. If you want the Rutgers name specifically, you think that name would be as valuable if they only offered YouTube links and no lectures?
Comment by ScarletGingerrr: I second you on this. Don't know why people are downvoting you when literally everyone ends up watching other Youtube videos on the topic, especially STEM courses and the professors style might not be for everyone. You go to lecture occasionally to get a basic sense of how well you need to know the topics taught and then you use your own time to learn and apply them effectively.
